MEDDICC.description: Kitewing's default qualification framework for deals above $25k ACV. Score each criterion 0-3: 0 unknown, 1 weak/assumed, 2 partially confirmed, 3 confirmed by the buyer.

criteria.name: Metrics
criteria.definition: Quantified outcomes the buyer expects (overtime, first-time-fix, drive time, invoice lag, DSO).
questions: If we fixed this, what number would move — and from what to what?
How do you measure technician productivity today (jobs per tech per day, first-time-fix)?
What does one extra hour of overtime cost you fully loaded?
How many days after a job does the invoice go out?

criteria.name: Economic buyer
criteria.definition: The person who can approve the spend and say yes when everyone else says no.
questions: Who signs off on a software investment of this size?
Has this person approved a similar project before? How did it go?
What would they need to see to say yes?
listen_for: A named person with budget authority
Access: will they join a call?
Approval thresholds (e.g. above $200k goes to the board)

criteria.name: Decision criteria
criteria.definition: The technical, commercial and vendor criteria the buyer will use to choose.
questions: What must the new system do on day one that the current one can't?
How important is offline mobile for your technicians?
Are there integration must-haves (accounting, identity, parts suppliers)?
Is there a price-per-technician ceiling you are working to?

criteria.name: Decision process (incl. paper process)
criteria.definition: The steps, people and dates between today and a signed contract, including legal, security and procurement.
questions: Walk me through how you will make this decision and by when.
Who else needs to see a demo or a reference?
What does legal and security review look like, and how long does it usually take?
What happens if the decision slips past your target date?
listen_for: A compelling event (end of support, peak season, renewal)

criteria.name: Identify pain
criteria.definition: The business pain, its cost, and why it must be solved now.
questions: What happens on your worst dispatch day?
What has this cost you in the last 12 months — lost contracts, overtime, late invoices?
Why solve it now rather than next year?
What have you tried already?

criteria.name: Champion
criteria.definition: An insider with influence who sells for us when we are not in the room and has something to gain.
questions: What would a successful project mean for you personally?
Who would push back, and how would you handle it?
Can you get us 20 minutes with the economic buyer?

criteria.name: Competition
criteria.definition: Other vendors, in-house builds and the status quo.
questions: Who else are you looking at?
What do you like about them?
What happens if you do nothing and extend the current system?

BANT.description: Lightweight framework for Starter deals and SDR qualification (below $25k ACV). Score each criterion 0-3.

criteria.name: Budget
criteria.definition: Money is available or can be found.
questions: Is there a budget set aside for this?
What do you spend today on the current tools and workarounds?

criteria.name: Authority
criteria.definition: We are talking to, or have access to, the decision maker.
questions: Who besides you is involved in the decision?
Who signs?

criteria.name: Need
criteria.definition: A real business problem we solve.
questions: What is the biggest scheduling or dispatch headache today?
What does it cost you?

criteria.name: Timeline
criteria.definition: A date by which they need a solution.
questions: When do you need this live?
What is driving that date?

hvac_plumbing.name: HVAC, plumbing & home services
pains: Peak-season overtime and Saturday dispatch shifts
Repeat visits because the wrong part was on the truck
Invoices sent days after the job
hypotheses: Overtime above 10% of tech hours in peak season
Invoice lag of 5+ days drives DSO above 45 days
Legacy dispatch tool nearing end of support
metrics_to_ask: drive hours per tech per day

facilities.name: Facilities management
hypotheses: SLA penalties paid in the last year
Technicians spend 20%+ of time on paperwork

fire_security.name: Fire protection, alarm & security
hypotheses: Missed or late inspections create liability
Inspection reports take days to reach customers

pest_landscaping.name: Pest control, landscaping & route-based services
hypotheses: Office admin time above 10 hours a week on rescheduling

stages.name: Prospecting
stages.exit_criteria: Meeting booked with someone who feels the pain.

stages.name: Discovery
stages.exit_criteria: Pain, metrics and a compelling event confirmed; economic buyer identified.

stages.name: Solution Validation
stages.exit_criteria: Tailored demo done; decision criteria and process confirmed; champion tested.

stages.name: Proposal
stages.exit_criteria: Proposal and ROI reviewed with the economic buyer.

stages.name: Negotiation
stages.exit_criteria: Verbal yes; legal and security review under way.

call_agenda_30min: 0-3 min: introductions, purpose, agenda and time check
3-15 min: current process, worst-day story, pain and what has been tried
15-22 min: impact — baseline metrics and cost of inaction
22-27 min: decision process, people, timeline and compelling event
27-30 min: agree a dated next step (demo, ROI workshop, meeting with the economic buyer)

Fieldnest.positioning: Low-cost tool for small contractors (sweet spot under 40 technicians).
Fieldnest.list_price: about $59 per technician per month (public pricing page)
landmine_questions: What happens to photos and signatures when a technician has no signal?
How will you bill 1,800 maintenance agreements every month?

ServiceGrid Pro.list_price: custom; typically $140+ per technician per month
landmine_questions: Can you be live before your next peak season?
What is your plan for June 2027 when support ends?

follow_up_rules: Send the recap email within 24 hours of the call.
Recap = their words for the pain, the metrics they gave, what we heard about the decision process, and one dated next step.
Never attach pricing to a first recap; offer a ballpark range only if they asked.
Attach at most one case study, matched to their segment.
